hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding layer normalization to memory slot embeddings before attention computation will stabilize the attention distribution and improve exact-match retrieval accuracy.
hypothesis.rationale: Associative retrieval tasks require discriminative attention over memory slots. Unnormalized memory embeddings can cause attention score instability, leading to diffuse or incorrect slot selection. Layer normalization standardizes the memory representations without adding significant parameters.
hypothesis.instruction: In modeling_rmt/huggingface_rmca_v3.py, locate the RMCAMemoryCell class. Add a nn.LayerNorm layer with embedding dimension after memory slots are retrieved/encoded but before the cross-attention computation. Apply this normalization to the memory key/value embeddings used in attention scoring.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding a learnable temperature parameter to the cross-attention softmax will sharpen attention distributions and improve exact-match retrieval accuracy.
hypothesis.rationale: Softer attention distributions cause the model to distribute probability mass across multiple memory slots, reducing confidence in correct selections. Sharper attention (via temperature scaling) concentrates probability on the most relevant slot, which is critical for exact-match accuracy in associative retrieval tasks.
hypothesis.instruction: In modeling_rmt/huggingface_rmca_v3.py, add a learnable temperature parameter (torch.nn.Parameter initialized to 1.0) to the CrossAttention class. In the compute_attention_weights method, multiply attention scores by this temperature before applying softmax normalization.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding learnable memory position embeddings to the cross-attention keys and values will help the model distinguish between different memory slots and improve associative retrieval accuracy.
hypothesis.rationale: Without explicit position information, the model may confuse which memory slot contains which association, especially when multiple similar items are stored. Adding position embeddings provides a unique identifier for each slot, enabling precise key-value matching during retrieval.
hypothesis.instruction: In modeling_rmt/huggingface_rmca_v3.py, modify the RMCAMemory class to: (1) Add a learnable parameter self.memory_pos_embeddings = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(num_memory_slots, hidden_dim)) in __init__, (2) In the forward method, add self.memory_pos_embeddings to the memory keys and values before computing cross-attention: keys = memory_keys + self.memory_pos_embeddings, values = memory_values + self.memory_pos_embeddings

hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding a learnable temperature scaling parameter to the cross-attention mechanism will sharpen attention distributions and improve retrieval precision for associative tasks.
hypothesis.rationale: The current cross-attention softmax may produce overly diffuse attention distributions that dilute signals from the correct memory slot. A learnable temperature parameter allows the model to dynamically sharpen attention, focusing more precisely on relevant memory entries during retrieval.
hypothesis.instruction: In modeling_rmt/huggingface_rmca_v3.py, modify the RMCAAttention class: (1) Add a learnable parameter 'attention_scale' initialized to 1.0 in __init__, (2) Modify the attention computation in forward method to divide attention logits by attention_scale before softmax, (3) Ensure attention_scale is registered as a parameter so it can be optimized during training.
